observations.body: Dashboard at /dashboard greets Emily and shows Leave balance 18 days and Pending leave requests 0. Navigation offers Dashboard, Directory, My Leave, Timesheet and My Profile; the page also shows Notifications (3), Request leave and Fill timesheet. The displayed product label is Employee v0.1.0.

Opening Directory first showed a Loading… state in the immediate capture, then settled at /directory with 28 employees, page 1 of 3 and a Next button. The visible list starts with Abigail Stone and includes Emily Dawson; a name search box and department selector are present.
The Directory link opened the Employee directory at /directory.

GET /api/employees returned HTTP 200 for the Directory load. The response reported total 28 employees, page 1 of 3, with 10 items in this page. The observed query was q="", department="", sort="name", dir="asc", page="1".
GET /api/employees?q=Emily Dawson&department=&sort=name&dir=asc&page=1 returned HTTP 200 with one matching employee, Emily Dawson in Engineering, total 1 and pages 1.
The department query parameter supports an HR filter combined with q.
GET /api/employees?q=Emily Dawson&department=HR&sort=name&dir=asc&page=1 returned HTTP 200 with items [], total 0, page 1 and pages 1.
An empty q value can be combined with department=HR for the employee list operation.

Employee directory displays 28 employees over 3 pages, with 10 visible on page 1. It offers a name search, a department selector with All departments, Engineering, Sales, Marketing, Finance and HR, a Name header showing ascending order, and Previous (disabled on page 1) and Next controls.
The shared navigation on Employee directory includes My Leave (/leave) and Dashboard (/dashboard).

Opening My Leave first showed the balance and an empty history while requests loaded, then settled at /leave with Available balance 18 days and one request: Aug 11–13, 2026, 3 Vacation days, approved with comment “Approved – enjoy!”.
The My Leave navigation opened the My leave page at /leave.

Searching for “Emily Dawson” sent GET /api/employees with q="Emily Dawson", empty department, sort=name, dir=asc and page=1. HTTP 200 returned total 1 and pages 1; the UI displayed one matching row for Emily Dawson in Engineering.
The Department selector includes HR as a choice and can be combined with the name search.
With the name query “Emily Dawson” active, selecting HR resulted in 0 employees, the row “No employees found,” and page 1 of 1.
The name search field can be empty while the HR department remains selected.
My leave shows an Available balance of 18 days, a Request history table, and a New request link to /leave/new. The history currently contains one approved Vacation request.
Opening New request displayed /leave/new with a leave type selector (Vacation selected), required Start date and End date fields, a Reason field, Submit request and Cancel.
The New request link opened the New leave request form at /leave/new.
The shared navigation on My leave includes Directory at /directory.
Opening Directory first showed Loading… in the immediate capture, then settled at /directory with 28 employees on page 1 of 3.
The Directory navigation opened Employee directory at /directory.

New leave request form offers Vacation (selected), Sick and Personal. Start date and End date are marked required and presented as read-only text inputs, with calendar selection implied by the control. Reason is optional. Submit request and Cancel buttons are visible. The form notes that weekends are not counted.
The Start date control opened a calendar showing September 2026 with previous/next month arrows and selectable day numbers 1–30.
Clicking Start date opened its calendar on September 2026. The date input remains blank until a day is selected.
Selecting the next-month arrow advanced the Start date calendar from September 2026 to October 2026; the date fields remain blank.
Selecting October 20 populated Start date as 2026-10-20 and closed the calendar; End date remains blank.
End date is read-only and opens its own calendar with previous/next month arrows and selectable days.
With Start date already set to 2026-10-20, opening End date displayed September 2026 and left End date blank.
Selecting the next-month arrow advanced the End date calendar from September 2026 to October 2026 while keeping Start date 2026-10-20 and End date blank.
Selecting October 21 populated End date as 2026-10-21 and displayed Duration: 2 days for the October 20–21 Vacation request.
The filled form shows Vacation, 2026-10-20 through 2026-10-21, Duration: 2 days, and the reason “Synthetic trial data: Perquiro Explore leave request.”
The current form is ready to submit once: Vacation from 2026-10-20 to 2026-10-21, displayed duration 2 days, reason marked as synthetic trial data. No request has been submitted yet.

Submitting the marked synthetic Vacation request produced HTTP 201 from POST /api/leave with record id 3, dates 2026-10-20 through 2026-10-21, 2 days and status pending. The settled My leave page shows balance 16 days and a pending 2-day row, but renders its range as Oct 20–Oct 20.
After POST /api/leave returned HTTP 201, the browser navigated from /leave/new to My leave at /leave and displayed the new pending request.

POST /api/leave accepted the UI request with HTTP 201. The observed request supplied type Vacation, startDate 2026-10-20, endDate 2026-10-21 and a synthetic trial reason. The response returned record id 3, 2 days, status pending, and the same dates.

GET /api/me returned HTTP 200 for Emily while opening My Leave. The response identified employee id 7, role employee and leaveBalance 18 at that time; unrelated personal fields are not copied into this inventory.

GET /api/leave returned HTTP 200 for the signed-in employee. After the synthetic submission, the list contained two requests: id 3, Vacation, 2026-10-20 through 2026-10-21, 2 days, pending; and id 1, Vacation, 2026-08-11 through 2026-08-13, 3 days, approved.
